subject: SignalForge integration — architecture fit & test plan
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@signalforge.io>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: marco.ruiz@signalforge.io
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SignalForge x Redwood — architecture fit and initial test plan

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking time earlier this week. SignalForge is moving forward with a proof-of-concept to embed Redwood-hosted inference into our event-driven pipeline (low-latency scoring at 100–200 qps, mixed short/long contexts). Before we hand this to engineering we want to validate a reference architecture and identify any compatibility or performance risks.

Attached is a short reference-arch sketch and our baseline integration test plan (very high level). Key asks:
- Can Redwood support a pinned model variant + fallback policy in the same region with predictable p95 latency under 100ms for short requests?
- Guidance on batching and caching strategies for our pattern (many repeated prefixes; heavy caching potential).
- Known limitations or recommended quantization/profile for the model family we plan to use.

Would you and your team be able to review and suggest a validation checklist we can run in a joint smoke test? Happy to schedule a 30–45m call next week.

Attachments: signalforge-redwood-reference-arch-v1.pdf, sf-integration-test-plan.xlsx

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
SignalForge Solutions
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@signalforge.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SignalForge x Redwood — architecture fit and initial test plan

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the docset, this is the right place to start. Looping in Hannah (solutions validation) and Lauren (partnerships engineering) to scope the joint validation.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Pinned variant + fallback: yes — we can pin a model variant within a region and configure automated fallback to a smaller/cheaper variant. We’ll want to validate that the fallback path preserves response schema and that KV cache warming is handled during failover.
- Batching & caching: your repeated prefix pattern is ideal for prefix caching + hot-key routing. We’ll propose a batching window that keeps p95 latency < 100ms at your expected short-request size.
- Quantization: we’ll recommend a 4-bit quantized variant for cost/performance trade-offs for your workload, and a full-precision variant for canary runs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Joint smoke test scope doc (we’ll create a checklist and share) — target: functional + latency gates.
2) Run small-scale load test in Redwood dedicated dev pool (non-prod) with mirrored traffic.
3) Iterate on batching/caching config and report.

Can you do Wed 25 Feb 10:00 PT for a quick sync? If that works, we’ll send a calendar invite and include a short pre-read.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@signalforge.io>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marco.ruiz@signalforge.io
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SignalForge x Redwood — architecture fit and initial test plan

Thanks — Wed 25 Feb 10:00 PT works for us (I’m in). I’ve added Marco (platform eng) to the thread; he’ll bring traffic-shaping details and the sample workloads.

One clarifying detail on the fallback behavior: when a pinned model is unavailable we need to ensure the observability surface clearly indicates which variant answered the request (metadata in response) to preserve auditability. Is that a standard field?

Also attaching a slightly updated test-plan with sample payload shapes and 95th/99th latency targets.

Attachments: sf-integration-test-plan.xlsx (updated)

— Alyssa
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@signalforge.io>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SignalForge x Redwood — architecture fit and initial test plan

Hi Alyssa / Marco — nice to meet you virtually. Per our sync this morning, I’m attaching a draft validation checklist and a short-run configuration that mirrors your sample workload (we used the sample payloads from your updated spreadsheet). Items included:
- Functional smoke tests (response schema, model-variant header, failover correctness)
- Latency gates (short requests p95 < 100ms, long requests p95 < 400ms)
- Cache-warming steps and expected hit rates
- Batching strategy and suggested window sizes by qps bucket
- Observability items: token-level cost breakdown, per-variant traces, and a response header (x-redwood-variant) that indicates which variant served the request

We validated the variant header in a quick lab run; it is present by default in our dev telemetry and we can surface it in your responses (x-redwood-variant) and in audit logs. We also note that if you use a dedicated pool with burst capacity toggled on, there is a short window where KV cache needs warming — we recommend a warmup traffic step in the checklist.

I’m available to run the smoke test together on Mon 1 Mar (dev pool booked) if that aligns with your schedule.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Validation Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Alyssa / Marco — quick status and action items following Hannah’s checklist:
1) We confirmed x-redwood-variant will be surfaced in responses and audit logs.
2) Draft validation checklist attached (signalforge-redwood-reference-arch-v1.pdf includes the sequence and the expected pass/fail gates).
3) Dev pool slot reserved for Mon 1 Mar 09:00 PT — Hannah will run the smoke test with your sample traffic.

Action items for SignalForge ahead of the run:
- Provide a 30-minute window of representative traffic for warmup (repeated prefixes included).
- Share any client-side retry/backoff logic you plan to use.
- Confirm whether you want 4-bit quantized variant active for cost run or stick to full-precision for the first canary.

We’ll capture results in JIRA PARTNER-392 and follow up with a short report and recommended config changes.

Thanks, looking forward to the run.
— Priyom
